主要内容: Mondelez CEO Irene Rosenfeld stated that the food industry is changing faster than ever before. She highlighted significant shifts in consumer behavior, retail environments, and competitive dynamics. Rosenfeld, who has led Mondelez since its spin-off from Kraft in 2012, emphasized the magnitude and speed of these changes, which she described as greater than any she has seen in her career. Her successor, Dirk Van de Put, will take over as CEO on November 20. Despite challenges such as evolving consumer preferences and the rise of e-commerce platforms like Amazon, Rosenfeld remains confident in the food industry and Mondelez's performance. In her final quarter as CEO, Mondelez reported earnings of 57 cents per share, exceeding Wall Street's estimate of 54 cents, and revenue of $6.53 billion, surpassing the $6.45 billion forecast. Rosenfeld attributed the strong results to the recovery of emerging markets and stable foreign exchange rates. She also noted that investments in brands and distribution channels are yielding positive returns. Rosenfeld advised Van de Put to focus on profitable growth and accelerating top-line expansion.
